title: Language features suit audience and purpose

draft.title: Language features suit audience and purpose
card: The audience is the group of people a text is written for. Writers think about their age, what they already know and what they care about.
The purpose is the reason a text is written, such as to inform, to persuade or to entertain.
Writers choose words, sentence length and features to suit both. A text for young children may use short sentences, simple words and bright pictures.
A report for adults may use longer sentences, technical words and headings. The same topic can read very differently for each audience.
draft.remember: Writers match their words and features to who will read the text and why.

a.q: Why would a writer use short sentences and simple words in a book about frogs?
opts: The audience is young children who are learning to read
The purpose is to give a detailed report to scientists
The audience already knows the technical words well
The purpose is to persuade adults to protect wetlands
a.why: Short sentences and simple words suit young readers who are still building their reading skills. A report for scientists would use longer sentences and technical words, so that option does not fit.
a.clue: Think about who finds short, simple sentences easiest to read.

b.q: Priya writes a notice for her school website that tells Year 12 students the exam times. Which choice best suits her audience and purpose?
opts: A clear list of dates and times under a heading
A funny story about an exam that went wrong
Long descriptions of how the exam room looks
A poem about how nervous students often feel
b.why: The purpose is to inform, so students need exam times they can find fast. A list under a heading does this. A funny story might entertain, but it would not tell students when to turn up.
b.clue: What does the reader need to find quickly?

a.best: The audience is young children who are learning to read

b.best: A clear list of dates and times under a heading
